answer: Hamas's 1988 Covenant says the land of Palestine is a waqf that may not be given up, that peaceful solutions contradict its principles, and quotes a saying about fighting Jews. Its 2017 document is milder: it accepts a state on the 1967 lines as a 'formula of national consensus' and says its conflict is with Zionism, not with Jews. But it still says there shall be no recognition of Israel and rejects any alternative to liberating Palestine 'from the river to the sea'. Our reading: Hamas uses the phrase for a claim to all the land, with no recognition of Israel.

facts.text: The 1988 Hamas Covenant says Palestine is an Islamic waqf that may not be given up, and that peaceful solutions and international conferences contradict the movement's principles. Two English translations were compared: the Avalon Project text (the Jewish Virtual Library's text is the same translation with American spelling; advocacy publisher, not counted) and the Federation of American Scientists' excerpts (a separate translation, translator not named). We did not find a third published translation (for example the Journal of Palestine Studies version of 1993).

contested.text: The 2017 document was a real moderation. Beverley Milton-Edwards (Brookings Doha Center) calls the revised charter 'a triumph of politics over resistance', and Azzam Tamimi, author of 'Hamas: A History from Within', says Hamas would prefer to say the old charter expressed Hamas in 1988 and that today's document speaks for it now.

contested.text: The 2017 document was not a real moderation. Udi Dekel (INSS) concludes that one must not recognise Israel 'not even in exchange for the establishment of a Palestinian state', and Abu Saada of Al-Azhar University is quoted as saying that while moderates can point to the 1967 state, hardliners can still say they are not recognising Israel.

could_not_verify: The 2017 document's Arabic original and Hamas's own site; the English text is quoted from Middle East Eye's full publication, which is a news site.
Whether Hamas ever formally repealed the 1988 Covenant: no source read says it did, and Azzam Tamimi says the 2017 text would only 'practically' replace it.
Scholars of the 2017 document: the RAND piece and a Times of Israel analysis could not be fetched. Each position in 'contested' rests on one think-tank paper and one quoted analyst in Al Jazeera.

Who translated the English texts: the Avalon and Jewish Virtual Library texts of the 1988 Covenant name no translator (and read almost identically); the FAS excerpts name none either; Middle East Eye's 2017 text names none. In the Avalon text, '(killing the Jews)' in Article 7 is a parenthesis inside the English translation; a disputed rendering that the card does not rest on.

Ghazi Hamad's words in Arabic, and any translation of the LBCI interview that is not MEMRI's. We searched for AP, Reuters, BBC, Guardian and NBC coverage of the interview and found none; the Newsmax, Ynetnews and National Desk items are one translation (declared as MEMRI wire), and the Jerusalem Post is the only outlet describing his reply to NBC in its own words. Reports differ on the interview date (24 October per MEMRI-based reports; one item dates it to 1 November), so the card says 'late October'. NBC's own transcript was not found.

The Las Vegas Review-Journal (a Newsmax story) does not name MEMRI; it is declared as the same MEMRI wire because its English wording matches MEMRI's as carried by The National Desk. The FAS excerpts page names no translator or author and frames the Covenant in its own editorial words, so it is kind other and does not count toward three sources.

The 'again and again' statement was moved out of the facts into 'contested' as one advocacy group's translation. We searched again (Arabic text, the channel's own pages, major outlets) and found no LBCI page, Arabic report or non-MEMRI translation of the interview.
A third, separate published translation of the 1988 Covenant (for example the Journal of Palestine Studies, 1993, or a university-press documentary history): not found online. Two were compared.

Not a position but an unverified report, so it is here and not in 'contested': in an Arabic interview on Lebanon's LBCI in late October 2023 Hamas politburo member Ghazi Hamad is quoted as saying 'we will do this again and again'. Every English report we read (Newsmax via the Las Vegas Review-Journal, Ynetnews, The National Desk) carries MEMRI's translation, MEMRI is an advocacy group, and the card does not treat the statement as established. A week later NBC asked him about it; the Jerusalem Post says he largely deflected, and Hot Air, quoting NBC, has him answer, 'What do you want us to do, stop?'
not_claimed: This card does not say that Palestinians as a people, or the PLO, hold Hamas's views; it describes Hamas's documents only.
It does not say that everyone who chants the phrase endorses Hamas.
It does not say Hamas has not changed at all: the 2017 document differs from the 1988 one, and the card lists how.
It does not quote Hamas's statements as a verdict on the war; Hamas's own leaders' words are cited as they were reported.

answer_claims.says: Hamas's 1988 Covenant says the land of Palestine is a waqf that may not be given up, that peaceful solutions contradict its principles, and quotes a saying about fighting Jews.
Its 2017 document is milder: it accepts a state on the 1967 lines as a 'formula of national consensus' and says its conflict is with Zionism, not with Jews.
But it still says there shall be no recognition of Israel and rejects any alternative to liberating Palestine 'from the river to the sea'.
Our reading: Hamas uses the phrase for a claim to all the land, with no recognition of Israel.

skeptic.notes: Round three (the last). Changed since round two: the 'again and again' statement is out of the facts. I judged that 'contested' is the wrong home (it is for positions people hold, not for one reported quote), so I moved it into could_not_verify, worded as an unverified report; the answer never relied on it. The Covenant facts 0 to 2 now say two translations were compared; I re-read both (Avalon and FAS) and each has the waqf, Article 13 'so-called peaceful solutions', the 'obliterate it' quotation, 'no solution except jihad' and the Article 7 saying, so the document wording is confirmed first-hand in two independent translations. Honest limit: the secondary sources on facts 0 to 2 (CFR, Middle East Institute, Wilson Center) describe the 1988 charter in general and do not repeat those articles, so the 'record' flag does not apply (it needs two sources reporting the same content); the gate's three are met, but the support for the specific articles is the document itself. A person who wants more could add a scholarly book quoting Articles 7, 11 and 13 (for example Hroub, Mishal and Sela). Scholars in contested are quoted from readable pages. Nothing in the facts is misleading and the card says what it could not find.

citer.notes: Round three: the answer is unchanged and never rested on the Hamad statement; answer_claims re-checked against the five facts (0 to 4) and stand.
